# Question: generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Answer

The strongest plausible shortcut is **collapse up/down-only symmetry into no
symmetry**.  The true rule classifies each tight binary motif as neither,
left/right-only, up/down-only, or both, then compares those classes.  The rival
uses the same procedure except that it maps the up/down-only class to “neither”
before forming the equality matrix.

This shortcut fits **4/4 canonical demonstrations and 5/5 canonical labelled
pairs**.  None of the canonical motifs is up/down-only, so the missing class-2
branch is observationally invisible there.  It is stronger than color, exact
shape, or position guesses because it performs the intended symmetry analysis on
every canonical case and omits only one unshown semantic branch.

I checked this through the public `arcpuzzles apply` path.  The retained report is
`checks/main-counterexample/racket.json`; it records generator SHA-256
`7f9c01a709cc923a4c9cd2c17a25065895d5dc1773c722e2f411bef306c8719c`, executed rule hash `ae585f1eb109`, input hash
`40d89a0f3ea735ca24a98e5224e7e851b21a9b90ded64a6e2c20016a6d99003f`, and output hash `69fb0e37bfee1ec13c8e13c421c1a81985feb601f84beafd3a13fe79b42f5507`.  The Python
rule mirror produces the same output, `self_check` accepts the input, and the
focused regression test reads the retained artifact and proves the rival differs.

The repaired generator **does emit these cases**.  Default curriculum slots 0
and 2 provide independent up/down-only witnesses, including class triples
`(2,2,0)` and `(0,2,2)`.  The final 300-lesson census used four demonstrations
plus one query per lesson, 100 lessons in each difficulty band, and held out every
one of the five labelled pairs as query.  The collapse rival was refuted in all
300 production lessons; all 1,500 query rotations were also unambiguous against
all three declared competitors.  This is finite declared-rival evidence, not a
proof of unique induction against every possible program.
